title: Tokyo Pilgrimage 東京巡礼
blurb: Walk the real Shibuya and Shinjuku, rebuilt from open data and lit by the real sun: the scramble, SHIBUYA SKY 229 m up, Sangenjaya's backstreets, Kabukicho's arch and the stairs of Suga Shrine, ten years after a film and a game made them famous.

travel.name: The 男坂, at the foot

npcs.name: Aoi 葵
npcs.role: Pilgrimage guide 聖地巡礼ガイド

Shibuya's scramble at {time}. {sun_line}

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: Every walk done. Report back to Aoi at Hachiko.

quests.title: Hachiko
talk: ようこそ渋谷へ! I'm Aoi. I guide pilgrims: people who come to stand where a story stood. This month it's ten years since a film and a game put these streets on the map.
This is the real Shibuya, rebuilt from open data: {buildings} buildings, {share:plateau}% of the footprint area at heights Project PLATEAU surveyed.
Hachiko has sat here since 1948. A game called this square Station Square. Walk out onto the scramble when the lights change.

steps.text: Meet Shun at the mouth of Center Gai

quests.title: Center Gai
talk: Center Gai. A game called it Central Street and gave it a burger bar that doesn't exist. The arch is real: go and read it.
See the glass passage over the crossing, on the station side? Okamoto Taro's thirty-metre mural, Myth of Tomorrow, hangs inside. A game made that passage a hideout.
For the view everyone came for, go up SHIBUYA SKY on top of Scramble Square. Yuna works the door.

steps.text: Read the arch over Center Gai
Find Yuna at SHIBUYA SKY's street door

quests.title: SHIBUYA SKY
talk: SKY GATE: the lifts run from 14F to 45F at 360 metres a minute. From the 46th floor an escalator takes you out into the open air.
The roof is about 2,500 square metres. The glass is lowest at SKY EDGE, over the scramble. No bags past 46F: the wind takes them.
Press E by the lift door. Or open the map: the roof is on your list of places to go.

steps.text: Ride the escalator out onto the roof
Stand at SKY EDGE, over the scramble

quests.title: SKY EDGE
talk: From up here the scramble is a clock face: everyone waits, then everyone goes.
GEO COMPASS, the raised deck in the middle, points at places you can't see: Mt Fuji, Skytree, Suga Shrine, even Paris and Sydney.
After dark, CROSSING LIGHT: eighteen searchlights. {sun_line}

quests.title: Sangenjaya
talk: Sangenjaya, three tea houses. In a game it's Yongen-Jaya, four: the same backstreets with one more tea house.
The game's café has the front of a snack bar here, New Marina. The bathhouse is Chiyo-no-yu, across the lane.
Take it slow. These are people's homes and small shops.

quests.title: Chiyo-no-yu
talk: Forty years a regular. The curtain says ゆ: hot water. Men on one side, women on the other.
Coin laundry beside it, vending machines out front. Everything a backstreet needs.
Come back after dark. The signs light up the triangle between Setagaya-dori and Route 246.

quests.title: The stairs
talk: 你好! I flew in from Shanghai for the tenth anniversary. These are the stairs from the poster: Suga Shrine's 男坂.
{landmark:suga.otokozaka.steps} steps, three and a half metres wide, red iron handrails on both sides and down the middle. Count them on the way up.

steps.text: Find Mr Sato by the torii

quests.title: Suga Shrine
talk: Suga Shrine has watched over Yotsuya's eighteen towns since 1634. The hall burned in the 1945 raids; the parishioners rebuilt it.
The great torii went up in 1990. The ema rack is full this year: a lot of them are for the film's tenth.
Read a few. Then, if you like, wait for dusk: the light the film was made of.

choices.text: Show me dusk on the stairs

steps.text: Read an ema on the rack
Stand at the foot of the stairs

quests.title: Shinjuku
talk: Shinjuku 2-chome: a few hundred bars, most of them the size of a living room. A game put a bar here where a journalist drank.
Kabukicho's arch has been red since 1969. Go and see it after dark, and say hello to Officer Ono at the koban.

quests.title: Kabukicho
talk: Kabukicho is named for a kabuki theatre planned here after the war. It was never built; the name stayed.
From the south side of the station you can see the Docomo tower's clock: {landmark:docomo.clock_d_m} metres across, {landmark:docomo.clock_z_m} metres up. You may know it from a film.

quests.title: Aoyama-itchome
talk: This is my stop. In a game a school stood up the road from here. There isn't one; I checked.
What's real: the ginkgo avenue of Meiji Jingu Gaien. 146 trees in four rows, nine metres apart, planted from 1908. They go yellow at the end of November.

steps.text: Walk the ginkgo avenue at Jingu Gaien

quests.title: Pilgrim
talk: お帰り! Stairs, a bathhouse, an arch, a roof 229 metres up. All of it real, all of it measured.
Ten years ago a film and a game drew these streets. Now you've walked them. Change the time, go up SHIBUYA SKY at night, or just wander.

spots.name: Ema rack 絵馬掛所
lines: 「君の名は。 公開10周年 おめでとう! 2016→2026」 (Your Name: happy 10th anniversary of the release!)
「10年経っても この階段で 胸がぎゅっとなる 2026.8.26」 (Ten years on, these stairs still squeeze my heart.)
「瀧くんと三葉が ずっと幸せで ありますように」 (May Taki and Mitsuha always be happy.)
「聖地巡礼 ついに来れた! 令和八年 夏」 (A pilgrimage: finally made it! Summer, Reiwa 8.)
「組紐みたいに ご縁が 結ばれますように」 (Like a braided cord, may our bond be tied.)
「大切な人の 名前を 忘れませんように」 (May I never forget the name of the one who matters.)
「彗星を観た夏から もう十年。 また会えますように」 (Ten years since the summer we saw the comet. May we meet again.)
「10周年の再上映 3回観ました! ありがとう」 (Saw the 10th-anniversary re-release three times. Thank you!)
「合格祈願 東京の大学に 行けますように 令和八年」 (Passing my exams: may I get into a university in Tokyo. Reiwa 8.)
「家内安全 健康第一 令和八年 丙午」 (Safety for the family, health first. Reiwa 8, year of the fire horse.)
「四ツ谷に越して一年 毎朝この坂を 上っています」 (A year since I moved to Yotsuya: I climb these stairs every morning.)
「劇場版 大ヒット祈願 制作スタッフ一同 2026」 (The film: praying for a big hit, from all the staff. 2026.)
「夕暮れの階段で 誰かとすれ違った 気がした」 (On the stairs at dusk I felt I passed someone.)
「初詣 2026 今年こそ 運命の人に 出会えますように」 (First visit of 2026: this year, may I meet the one.)
「就職成就 令和八年」 (A job offer, please. Reiwa 8.)
「三葉ちゃん 大好き♡ 10th anniversary」 (Mitsuha, I love you. 10th anniversary.)
「新海監督 素敵な十年を ありがとう」 (Director Shinkai: thank you for a wonderful ten years.)
「ずっと探してた この景色。 来てよかった」 (The view I was always looking for. Glad I came.)
「かたわれ時に また来ます 2026.10」 (I'll come back in the twilight. October 2026.)
「Persona5の聖地から Your Nameの聖地へ 東京巡礼 2026」 (From Persona 5's holy ground to Your Name's: a Tokyo pilgrimage, 2026.)
「《你的名字》 十周年快乐! 终于站在这段阶梯上 2026.8」 (Your Name: happy 10th! Finally standing on these stairs. August 2026.)
「希望我也能 遇见命中注定的 那个人」 (May I, too, meet the person meant for me.)
「从上海来 十年了 还是会哭」 (Came from Shanghai. Ten years, and I still cry.)
「愿所有相遇 都不被遗忘 2026 须贺神社」 (May no meeting ever be forgotten. Suga Shrine, 2026.)
「家人平安 工作顺利 2026」 (Peace for my family, work going well. 2026.)
「你的名字 十週年快樂 從台北來朝聖 2026.10」 (Your Name: happy 10th! A pilgrimage from Taipei. October 2026.)
「希望能和 那個人再次相遇 ♡」 (May I meet that person again.)
「너의 이름은 10주년 축하해! 2026」 (Your Name: happy 10th anniversary!)
「드디어 왔다 스가 신사 계단 꿈이 이루어졌어요」 (Finally here: the Suga Shrine stairs. A dream come true.)
「Happy 10th anniversary, Your Name! Melbourne 2026」
「Climbed the stairs at dusk. Still looking for someone.」
「10 years, 1 comet, a million goosebumps.」
「May we always find each other. 2026」
「¡10 años de Kimi no Na wa! México 2026」 (Ten years of Kimi no Na wa! Mexico, 2026.)
「Dix ans déjà… merci pour ce film. Paris 2026」 (Ten years already... thank you for this film. Paris, 2026.)
「Thanks for the magic, Suga-jinja!」
「商売繁盛 令和八年」 (Prosperity in business. Reiwa 8.)
「交通安全 令和八年 四谷」 (Road safety. Reiwa 8, Yotsuya.)
「猫のミケが 元気で いますように」 (May Mike the cat stay well.)
「東京に来て十年 あの映画が 背中を押してくれた」 (Ten years in Tokyo: that film gave me the push.)

spots.name: Offering box 賽銭箱
lines: Bow twice, clap twice, bow once. A coin first: five yen, go-en, sounds like 'a bond'.
Suga Shrine enshrines Susanoo and the Inari kami. It has watched over Yotsuya's eighteen towns since 1634.

spots.name: Temizuya 手水舎
lines: Left hand, then right, then a sip from your cupped left palm, never from the ladle. Then rinse the handle.

spots.name: 男坂 Otokozaka
lines: The 男坂: 52 stone steps, 18, 16 and 15 to the approach and 3 more, 3.6 m wide, red iron handrails both sides and down the middle.
Here each riser is 14 cm: 6.8 m from the street to the shrine, by GSI's laser survey of the ground.

spots.name: Hachiko 忠犬ハチ公
lines: Hachiko, an Akita, met his master here every evening. After Professor Ueno died in 1925 he kept coming, for almost ten years.
The first statue (1934) went for metal in the war; this is the 1948 recast. 'Meet at Hachiko' is still how Tokyo says 'meet at Shibuya'.

spots.name: Center Gai センター街
lines: SHIBUYA CENTER-GAI: a few hundred metres of shops, ramen and arcades from the scramble towards Udagawacho. A game knew it as Central Street.

spots.name: Chiyo-no-yu 千代の湯
lines: 千代の湯, a neighbourhood sentō. The curtain says ゆ, hot water. Tokyo sets the price of a bath at every sentō in the city.
Coin laundry beside it, vending machines out front: everything a backstreet needs. A game put its bathhouse here, across from the café.

spots.name: Vending machines 自販機
lines: A can of cold green tea rolls out. 150 yen.
Hot milk tea in a can. In October, already.
A bottle of water. There are about two million of these machines in Japan.

spots.name: New Marina ニューマリーナ
lines: A snack bar: a counter, a few stools, karaoke, a mama-san. A game borrowed this front for its café; the café isn't here, this is somebody's bar.
Upstairs next door, a café in an old house. Keep your voice down: people live in these lanes.

spots.name: Niku no Hanamasa 肉のハナマサ
lines: 肉のハナマサ: a meat-first supermarket, open 24 hours. The game's supermarket sits where this one does, with another name.

spots.name: Kabukicho Ichibangai 歌舞伎町一番街
lines: The red arch has stood at Kabukicho Ichibangai since 1969. Kabukicho is named for a kabuki theatre planned here after the war and never built.

spots.name: GEO COMPASS
lines: GEO COMPASS, the highest point of SHIBUYA SKY: the floor points the way to places out of sight.
Mt Fuji 富士山: 94 km at 250°  ·  Tokyo Skytree: 11 km at 59°  ·  Tokyo Tower: 3.9 km at 89°  ·  Suga Shrine: 3.5 km at 31°  ·  Osaka: 396 km at 255°
Kyoto: 365 km at 260°  ·  Hong Kong: 2,882 km at 246°  ·  Sydney: 7,822 km at 170°  ·  Melbourne: 8,188 km at 176°  ·  Paris: 9,717 km at 334°

spots.name: CLOUD HAMMOCK
lines: You lie back in the net. 229 metres up, nothing over you but the sky, and the wind.
Pilgrim
Here! This is the angle from the poster.
Friend
Stand on the left. I'll be halfway up.
Pilgrim
Ten years... I was in high school.
Student
Meet at Hachiko? Everyone says that.
Friend
Which side of Hachiko, though?
Student
The side with the tourists.
Visitor
Wait for green... now!
Visitor
All the lights go green at once: every way, even across.
Friend
Don't stop in the middle for a photo!
Friend
Ramen or monja?
Friend
Ramen. Then the arcade.
Friend
You always say that.
(from inside) Ka-kon... a wooden bucket on tiles.
Regular
Ahh. Just right.
Regular
Same as always?
Mama-san
Same as always.
Friend
Karaoke till the first train?
Friend
The first train's at five...
Friend
Exactly.
Visitor
You can see the scramble breathing.
Visitor
Is that Mt Fuji? Left, look.
Friend
Only on a clear day.
